subject: POC traffic profiling: concurrency & burst gating — next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nadia Zaman <nadia.z@oliveai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T16:15:00Z
Subject: POC traffic profiling: concurrency & burst gating — next steps

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete runbook for the POC probe. TL;DR: we can run a staged probe next week (canary -> soak -> stress) to validate concurrency gating and KV-cache behavior under your two primary user journeys.

What we agreed on (please correct if I misread):
- Baseline sustained RPS: 120 req/s (90% of traffic)
- Medium burst: 600 req/s for 30s (expected chat spikes)
- Peak burst: 2,400 req/s for 10s (edge case, <1% traffic)
- Typical input token distribution: mean 65 tokens, 90th percentile 180 tokens, max 1,024 tokens
- Concurrent sessions to size for: 220 concurrent streams (session-based KV reuse)
- Latency targets (success criteria): 95th percentile request-to-first-byte < 180 ms for baseline; 99th percentile < 350 ms during medium bursts
- Quality acceptance: system output parity vs production model (we'll run sampling-based evaluation; threshold: BLEU/ROUGE relative drift < 3% and manual check on 50 prompts)

Action items / ownership
- Redwood to produce an ingestion script and workload CSV with RPS/concurrency schedule: Hannah (owner) — attached template.
- Olive to provide representative session logs + example prompt buckets: Nadia (owner).
- Redwood infra to provision canary pool and a dedicated quantized model variant for the test: Karthik (owner).
- Schedule: Canary + short soak: target window Nov 9–10; full stress window Nov 11 (all times TBD).

Attachments: [Attachment: olive_poc_workload_template.csv (CSV)], [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx (DOCX)]

Notes/risks:
- When we hit 2,400 req/s bursts we'll likely rely on autoscaling + fallback routing to a smaller-context model; we recommended exercising that fallback in the stress window to validate graceful degradation.
- KV cache warmup is important — add a 5–10 minute pre-warm step in the canary.

Please reply with any edits to the runbook or alternative windows. If that looks right, I'll publish a short HubSpot timeline and ping procurement for SOW routing.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Nadia Zaman <nadia.z@oliveai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Price <sam.price@oliveai.com>, OliveAI Procurement <procurement@oliveai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T18:40:00Z
Subject: Re: POC traffic profiling: concurrency & burst gating — next steps

Thanks Hannah — that summary matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from product/ops: 

- Traffic classes: we have two main user journeys: 
  1) Quick lookup chat (mean tokens ~30, very low latency sensitive)
  2) Document summarization (mean tokens ~220, high compute per request)
- For the canary we want to validate both classes independently (short/long token profiles) and then run a mixed workload that approximates production blend (70% quick lookup / 30% summarization).

Acceptance tweaks:
- For summarization flows, given long contexts, can we target 99th percentile < 450 ms during medium bursts (we expect variance here)?
- For overall availability during the stress window we need no more than 0.4% error rate (5xx or model OOM).

Schedule constraints: procurement needs a week to sign the SOW for the dedicated probe; if we want the Nov 9 window we need a short trial SOW by EOD Nov 3. I uploaded a short traffic sample to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_olive-poc-plan 

Attached a zipped extract of session examples — these are redacted, but should be a good starter set.

Attachment: [olive_sample_session_logs.zip]

Nadia
Nadia Zaman
Head of Product Operations, OliveAI
nadia.z@oliveai.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nadia Zaman <nadia.z@oliveai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: POC traffic profiling: concurrency & burst gating — next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Nadia — that helps. Updated plan below with explicit probe phases and gating rules. Quoting your timing ask for the SOW.

Updated probe plan (canary -> soak -> stress):
1) Canary (Nov 9 morning local): 10 minutes, single-node pool, quick lookup profile only, verify KV-cache warmup and baseline latency. Success: <180 ms P95 on quick lookup; no 5xx. Owner: Hannah.
2) Soak (Nov 9 afternoon): 60 minutes, multi-node pool, mixed workload (70/30), validate autoscaling triggers, KV-cache hit-rate target >= 65% after warmup. Success: sustained CPU/GPU utilization within expected band, <0.2% errors. Owner: Monica.
3) Stress (Nov 11): three 10-minute bursts — medium (600 rps), peaker (2,400 rps), and a mixed ramp. Validate fallback routing and model variant latency. Success: overall error rate <0.4%, summarization 99th <450 ms. Owner: Karthik.

Notes on measurement and telemetry:
- We'll capture token-level latency, per-request model variant used, KV cache hit/miss, and per-route cost estimate. We'll provide a post-run report with time-series and a CSV of sampled prompts and outputs for your QA.
- HubSpot record created: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/87654321/deal/DEAL-2027-OLIVE-01 

Procurement: if you can get the short SOW to us by EOD Nov 3 we can push the canary into Nov 9 as planned. I'll draft a minimal SOW and route to Karthik for sign-off on infra sizing.

On the quantization note — Karthik, we'll probably run both int8-quant and fp16 variants during the stress window; can you confirm estimated per-request memory and if we need an extra 2GB per GPU for long contexts?

Onwards — I attached the workload template again and a one-page mutual action plan for procurement to sign.

Attachments: [olive_poc_workload_template.csv], [mutual_action_plan.docx]

Best,
Hannah

——
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: POC traffic profiling: concurrency & burst gating — next steps

Quick internal confirmation: we can provision the canary and two stress shapes (S1: 8xA100, S2: 32xA100 pool) for Nov 9–11. Memory note: for 1,024 token contexts with int8 quant we need approx 6.5GB of GPU memory per model instance plus ~2GB headroom for session KV. I'll set up a short runbook to toggle quantization profiles during the stress window.

I'll also pre-create the DocuSign SOW draft and loop procurement once Hannah drops the minimal SOW — ping me when it's ready and I'll route.
